Early user praised Customer.io as an email marketing system 'designed for the data-savvy marketer' with intuitive workflow building/editing/previewing, easy signup, no long-term contract, and fair usage-based pricing that let them go fully operational in two weeks.

After a change (possibly Series A), user complains of: price hikes based on contact count rather than actual email usage, unsolicited AE outreach, being forced onto annual commitment plans, removal of self-serve sign-in/testing, and annual AE calls with 'fake promises' to get signatures. Ultimately leaving the product.
Customer.io published a blog post titled 'Customer.io Actions – Why did we do it this way?' explaining design decisions, shared and discussed on HN.

Discussion references a Customer.io extended outage tied to FoundationDB, noting sympathy for how frustrating it must be for Customer.io given FoundationDB's acquisition by Apple limiting support responsiveness.
'We used customer.io for the past few months but due to bugs with the system, we switched to sendwithus with sendgrid as our ESP. We've been really happy with the results.'
Developer built an open-source alternative 'after getting frustrated with Customer.io's limitations,' citing desire for code-based marketing automation (SQL segments, TypeScript flows) as motivation.
